messages.subject: Poisson regression & corpus data
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm somewhat stuck with a, probably relatively trivial, question on Poisson regressions and corpus data. It seems that a requirement of the Poisson regression is to always use raw counts. In corpus linguistics, however, how do we deal with frequencies that come from corpora of different sizes? I would like to fit a Poisson regression model where the frequency of a linguistic item (the preposition 'into') is my dependent variable, and the corpus (6 corpora representing different varieties of English: ICE-GB, ICE-USA, ICE-HK, ICE-IND, ICE-SIN and a comparable corpus of Dutch English) is my independent variable. However, my corpus sizes vary between approximately  400,000 and 500,000 words, and the raw frequencies of the linguistic item can therefore not be taken at face value. The only source that I found that somewhat indirectly discusses this is Baayen (2008) who specifies that the raw frequencies used in a particular study comparing corpora are the frequencies out of the first 1.5million words of each corpus (so, in effect, this comes down to some normalisation and comparability of the raw frequencies… But this would be more difficult with the corpora I'm using since they are not homogeneous in terms of genres, and taking the first 400,000 words would cause some skew in the genres represented). Does it then make sense, in such a case, to normalize all frequencies in relative frequencies per 400,000 words (which comes closest to the observed frequencies without inflating them) and run the Poisson regression on those values? Or is there another - more 'principled' - way to deal with this? 

Thanks a lot in advance for in any  tips :-)

Samantha

messages.subject: Re: [StatForLing with R] Poisson regression & corpus data
parts:
Not a trivial question at all ... you can use the offset argument to
glm to include the corpus sizes in the comptuation, then it all works
as expected. I have one or two overview papers in the pipeline that
use this but since I don't know the final shape of them yet (one, I
have been waiting for a review for I think a YEAR!), those are not yet
available ...
